_comment: Claude Code telemetry settings for AI Catalyst, as an `env` fragment to MERGE
into the DevNext workspace policy at /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json.
This is not a standalone settings file — do not replace the policy with it.
MERGING THIS: only the keys below belong in the policy. The "//" keys are
commentary; merged literally they become environment variables named //, //_
and so on in every session. Drop them.
Verify with: /dplc-preflight otel   (reports question 5b for this harness)
WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SET
It sets nothing about LOGS. Not the logs exporter, not a logs endpoint, and
none of OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS / _ASSISTANT_RESPONSES / _TOOL_CONTENT /
_RAW_API_BODIES / _TOOL_DETAILS. Those are the enterprise's call, not
Catalyst's: prompt and tool logging may be required for security monitoring,
and it is not this project's place to switch that off. An earlier revision of
this fragment set all of them to "0", which was overreach.
WHY METRICS ONLY, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN
Catalyst needs one thing from telemetry: which skills and agents ran. Those
ride on `skill.name`, `agent.name`, `plugin.name` and `marketplace.name`,
which are attributes on the `cost.usage` and `token.usage` METRICS — no
content switch enables them and no log record is required to read them.
User prompts, assistant responses, tool content and command lines are only
ever emitted as LOG records. They are never metric attributes.
So pointing only the METRICS signal at the Catalyst collector makes it
*structurally* incapable of receiving prompt text. Not 'configured not to' —
incapable, because the signal that carries content is not sent there at all.
That guarantee survives someone later turning a content switch on, which a
policy of four zeroes does not.
THE ONE THING THAT WOULD BREAK IT
Do NOT set the generic OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to the Catalyst collector.
The generic variable is the fallback for EVERY unset signal, so with prompt
logging on it would route prompt text to us. Use the metrics-specific
variable, which is what this fragment does, and leave the generic one either
unset or pointed at the enterprise's own destination.
Concretely: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT is safe here.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is not.
